subject: Brokered DB outage window allocation — request for recalculation
messages:
From: Sally Tran <sally.tran@spincloud.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 22:48:00 +0000
Subject: Unexpected availability impact during your brokered DB maintenance window

Hi Diego,

We spotted a significant spike in latency and a small but steady stream of 500s for our integration with Redwood between 22:05–22:40 UTC last night. Our SRE team correlated the timeline and found a maintenance advisory from our DB broker (attachment: maintenance-notice-spincloud.pdf) that overlaps with your reported maintenance window, but SpinCloud believes the primary cause is an internal sequencing problem on Redwood's side rather than the broker.

Per our contract, SpinCloud is asking for a recalculation of the uptime tally for August with an allocation that treats the 22:10–22:30 segment as a Redwood-credited partial degradation rather than a third-party exclusion. That would impact our monthly credits and the renewal conversation.

Can you please share the probe logs and how Redwood arrived at the exclusion decision? We need the detailed timeline to take back to procurement.

Thanks,
Sally
Sally Tran
Head of Platform Reliability, SpinCloud


PS: I attached our maintenance notice and a short ops timeline for your reference.

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Sally Tran <sally.tran@spincloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 01:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected availability impact during your brokered DB maintenance window

Hi Sally — thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the SpinCloud notice.

We're looking into the overlap now. At a high level: our SLA model allows for third-party maintenance to be excluded when the primary failure vector is caused by a partner-scheduled maintenance and we have probes showing client routing change. However, we also want to be fair — if the behavior was partial degradation caused by our routing or cache eviction, we should not exclude it fully.

I'll loop in Marissa (ops) and Jonas (runtime) to pull the probe logs and timeline. Kimberly from legal is CC'd for contract/credit language implications. Expect a consolidated timeline and suggested allocation by EOD our time.

Appreciate the patience —
Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, Sally Tran <sally.tran@spincloud.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: brokered DB outage window allocation — probe and metric dump

Hi all — attaching probe_logs_20270831.csv and a short analysis (service-metrics-window-analysis.pdf). Summary below.

Summary:
- Observed client-facing error spike: 22:06–22:36 UTC (peak 22:14–22:20).
- Our distributed probes show an upstream 502/504 surge beginning 22:10 on the brokered DB path, coincident with SpinCloud's maintenance start.
- However, we also observed an increased KV cache miss rate on our inference routing pool starting ~22:08, with sustained elevated CPU on a subset of serving hosts until ~22:28.
- Traffic distribution: ~78% of affected requests took the primary brokered path; ~22% failed earlier in our edge routing layer with timeouts/retries.

Interpretation: this looks like a hybrid event. The broker maintenance contributed to the backend errors, but there is evidence our edge routing and cache behavior amplified the impact — producing partial degradation for those earlier time segments.

Proposed allocation for credit calculation:
- 22:06–22:10 UTC: classify as "partial degradation attributable to Redwood" (no third-party exclusion).
- 22:10–22:28 UTC: split 60/40 in favor of the broker (i.e., 60% third-party exclusion, 40% Redwood responsibility) given probe correlation and backend 502s.
- 22:28–22:36 UTC: broker resolved; classify residual noise as no-credit (below SLO thresholds).

If SpinCloud disagrees with the split, we can bring in joint packet-exchange logs and correlate request IDs.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Ops Analyst, Redwood Inference

Attachments: probe_logs_20270831.csv, service-metrics-window-analysis.pdf

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Sally Tran <sally.tran@spincloud.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: brokered DB outage window allocation — legal/contract note

Hi Sally and team,

Two quick points from the contract clause (section 4.3.2):
1) Third-party maintenance exclusion applies when the partner provides notice >= 72 hours and the failure trace is exclusively on the partner's infrastructure.
2) For hybrid events, our standard practice (and contract interpretation) is to apportion credits based on measurable impact. We usually avoid 100% exclusion when our telemetry shows amplifying factors.

Given Marissa's proposed split, legal is comfortable moving forward with a proportional credit calculation rather than full exclusion. We'll document the rationale so audit trails are clean for renewals.

If SpinCloud needs a formal written concession, we can prepare an email notice and the resulting credit calculation for SpinCloud procurement.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Sally Tran <sally.tran@spincloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: brokered DB outage window allocation — proposed settlement

Hi Sally — following up with our proposed path forward after internal review:

1) Allocation: per Marissa's analysis, Redwood will treat 22:06–22:10 UTC as Redwood-responsible partial degradation. For 22:10–22:28 UTC we propose a 60/40 split in favor of the broker (i.e., Redwood accepts 40% of culpability for that interval). The remaining minutes fall below credit thresholds.

2) Credit calculation: We'll run the standard SLO credit formula with the apportionment above and issue a one-time customer credit applied to your September invoice. Kimberly will include the legal rationale in the memo we send to procurement.

3) Technical follow-up: Jonas can schedule a joint postmortem call with SpinCloud SREs to exchange request IDs and packet capture windows (deferred until you approve the meeting). This will help avoid similar hybrid-amplifier cases in the future.

If SpinCloud is OK, we'll produce a formal PDF breakdown + accounting entry by EOD Friday and send it to procurement. Thank you for raising this quickly — we want renewal conversations to be based on a fair accounting.

Best,
Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sally Tran <sally.tran@spincloud.com>

Cc: ops@spincloud.com
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Brokered DB outage window allocation — request for recalculation

Diego — thanks for the detailed analysis and the allocation proposal. Procurement will review the credit memo; we also accept a joint postmortem to tighten the failure domain boundaries.

Two asks before we close:
- Please include the per-minute credit math in the memo so procurement can reconcile quickly.
- Can Jonas include at least one sample request ID mapping (we'll redact payloads) so our SREs can validate the 60/40 allocation at the request level?

If you provide those items, SpinCloud will accept the settlement and we can close the incident.

Regards,
Sally
